what_this_is: How this folder reads techniques and crosses them with a goal: which row fields hold which shared vocabulary, which words of a row the writer model reads, the instructions and worked examples it follows, and how many of each thing come back. Changing how techniques are described or crossed is editing this file, not the code.

bound.comment: The two row fields whose values are terms of a shared vocabulary: `why` holds the reasons a technique works, `changes` the properties it changes. Each need is tagged with a term of needs_tagged_by, so one row's change can be joined to another row's need.

vocabulary_lines.comment: The admission lines a new vocabulary starts with, for the meaning they were measured with (measure-reuse-line.mjs over reuse-line-pairs.json, 2026-10-30). The least close 'same' pair was 0.439 and the closest 'different' pair 0.713 ('perceived effort / perceived value': a shared word pulls terms together), so at or above reuse_at a proposal is the same term without asking, below new_below it is new without asking, and in between the writer judges. Another model or form needs its own measurement.

mechanism.says: Why a technique works, in words about what it does to a person or a system, never about the medium it was found in.

property.says: The abstract property of a person or a system that a technique changes or needs, such as attention over time, trust, perceived effort, recognisability or reproducibility.

reading.comment: The words of a source row the writer reads: these fields first, then any other string field, each cut to max_chars, the whole row to row_max_chars. Rows per call and the nearest existing terms shown per row (the model reuses them when they mean the same).

say_why.system:
You describe techniques so they can be reused in any medium. For each row, write:
- mechanism: 1 or 2 reasons WHY it works, each a short term (1-4 words) and says (one plain sentence about what it does to a person's mind or to a system). Never mention the medium (video, slide, page, code, camera) in a mechanism.
- operates_on: 1 or 2 abstract properties it changes, each a short term and says (what the property is).
- needs: 1 to 3 preconditions, each one short medium-free phrase.
- produces: 1 or 2 effects, each one short medium-free phrase.
- from_medium: the medium or field the row was found in, 1-4 words.
Terms: when one of the EXISTING terms listed for a row means the same thing, write that exact term and leave says empty. Coin a new term only when none of them fits, and then write its says. Prefer the general term a psychologist, designer or engineer would use. Write in plain British English. Return exactly one entry per row id, in order.

rows.text: name: Mirror format: two identical people, one small repeated change, a counter, and the viewer sees themselves | kind: format | description: Two figures start identical at week 1. A visible counter advances. One adds a small fixed step each week and the other does not; by week 13 the gap is large. The viewer realises they are the one who did not.
name: Crash zoom in | kind: camera-move | description: Punchy near-instant zoom snap onto the target, used for sudden emphasis.

name: Check that users can still succeed, as a third gate beside CI and CD | kind: principle | description: CI proves the code, CD proves the deploy; a third check proves that the intended person can still finish the intended task on the running product.

mechanism.says: The person reads themselves as the subject, so the outcome shown feels like their own future.

operates_on.says: How much a person feels something is about them.
How real the future result of a choice feels now.

needs: two cases identical except for one change
a result that grows visibly over repeated steps
an audience that recognises itself in the side that did nothing
produces: the person sees their own inaction as the cause of a worse outcome
an urge to adopt the one change

mechanism.says: A sudden jump in scale or speed forces attention onto one thing.

needs: calmer moments around it so the jump stands out

mechanism.says: Checking that the intended person can still reach the intended result, not only that the parts are correct.

needs: a named person and task that define success
a way to run that task on the real thing
produces: failures that matter to people are caught before they reach them

rows.text: name: 1-Bit Dithering | kind: historical-effect | category: 1980s | description: A picture built only from black and white pixels, where tone comes from how densely the dots are packed. Look for stippled textures that blend into gray at a distance.

name: A day of meals as a six-slide carousel | kind: format | description: Slide 1 is a lifestyle cover; slides 2 to 5 are one meal each in day order; slide 6 is the product. Six slides is short enough that most people reach the end, where the offer sits.

name: Tie each effect to the words it answers, not to seconds | kind: technique | description: Write the words alone, then attach each reveal, cut or graphic to the phrase it responds to. When the words change, everything tied to them moves with them.

mechanism.says: A look tied to a past period makes a person feel that period and what they link with it.
Fine patterns the eye blends are read as smooth tone.

operates_on.says: Which memories, feelings or periods a thing calls up.

needs: an audience that knows the era's look
produces: rich tone from only two values

mechanism.says: A series that is visibly short and ordered pulls the person through to its end.
Giving something useful first makes the offer that follows feel earned.

operates_on.says: How open a person is to being asked to buy or act.

needs: useful items that fit a familiar order
an offer that continues the same topic
produces: most people reach the last item, where the offer sits

mechanism.says: Tying each effect to the content it answers keeps them aligned when the content changes.

needs: content split into units that effects can point at
produces: changes to the content carry every dependent effect with them

same_meaning.system: You decide whether a proposed term means the same thing as one of a few existing terms of a shared vocabulary. Same means a person would use them interchangeably to explain why something works; related or overlapping is not the same. Answer with the exact existing term, or an empty string when none means the same.

needs_tags.comment: A need is tagged with the closest property at least tag_min close in meaning. Measured with embeddinggemma at 768 dims over need-tag-pairs.json (2026-10-30: 11 right tags 0.468-0.543, 11 wrong ones 0.450-0.549); the line misplaces 2 of 22, so a tag is a lead for pairing, never a fact.

cross.wants_system: You turn a goal into what must happen for it to succeed. Write 4 to 6 wants. Each want is one plain sentence about what must happen in the mind of the person the goal is for (or in the system it runs on), never about a medium, a format or a feature. Cover the whole path that person takes, choosing the steps that matter for this goal: noticing it and staying with it, seeing that it is about them and their own situation, understanding it, believing it, and doing what the goal needs. For each want, list 1 to 3 properties from the properties you are given (copy each term exactly) whose change makes the want happen. Respect the constraints. Example: for 'the first lesson of a language course' a want is 'the learner feels they can already say something useful', with the properties for how much effort it seems to take and how much progress is felt.
cross.pick_system: You choose why-it-works mechanisms for a goal. For each want you are given candidate mechanisms (term and what it does), found in techniques from many media. Pick up to 3 per want that would most directly make that want happen for this goal, in the goal's own medium; copy each term exactly. A mechanism may serve the goal even when its techniques came from a very different medium: judge what it does to a person or a system, not where it was found. Pick none for a want when none fits.
cross.adapt_system: You adapt techniques found in other media to one goal. For each item write one concrete line: exactly what to do in the goal's own medium, naming the real element to make (a headline, a screen, a step, a slide), never the original medium. For a pair, write one line that uses both together. Leave ruled_out_by empty. Only when a constraint makes an item impossible (not merely less useful), write an empty line and put that constraint, word for word, in ruled_out_by.

limits.comment: wants: most wants kept; candidates_per_want: mechanisms shown per want, the ones spanning most media first; picks_per_want: most mechanisms kept per want; techniques: most techniques returned; per_mechanism: most rows per picked mechanism; pairs: most pairs.
